summary: Word snapshot geometry consumers retain physical measurements at the OpenDocument boundary.

changes.new: WordDocument.ToOpenDocument(WordOpenDocumentConversionOptions options[, out OfficeConversionReport report], CancellationToken) : OdtDocument; ToOpenDocumentAsync; SaveAsOpenDocument(path | stream); SaveAsOpenDocumentAsync
changes.reason: Converters use the shared shape: To{Target}(options[, out OfficeConversionReport], ct), To{Target}Async returning OfficeConversionResult<T>, and SaveAs{Target}(path | stream) returning OfficeConversionReport. Result, Bytes and Stream twins are removed.
changes.replacement: The out report is the typed OdfConversionReport with per-feature mappings.

changes.new: OdtDocument.ToWord(WordOpenDocumentConversionOptions options[, out OfficeConversionReport report], CancellationToken); ToWordAsync; SaveAsWord(path | stream); SaveAsWordAsync
changes.reason: Converters use the shared shape: To{Target}(options[, out OfficeConversionReport], ct), To{Target}Async returning OfficeConversionResult<T>, and SaveAs{Target}(path | stream) returning OfficeConversionReport. Result, Bytes and Stream twins are removed.
Both directions share every setting, so one options type stays; LossPolicy keeps its three levels instead of FailOnLoss.

extraChanges.old: Word-to-ODT inline image export treats snapshot pixels as points; ODT-to-Word import wraps source points as pixels.
extraChanges.new: Convert physical image lengths to explicit points only at the ODF boundary and retain point dimensions when importing to Word.
extraChanges.reason: The snapshot geometry migration exposed reciprocal unit interpretation errors. Preserve actual image frames in either conversion direction, including independently authored input.
extraChanges.note: The existing ODT image-order workflow now checks centimeter-sized image frames after native Word save/load and ODT save/load, so reciprocal scale errors cannot cancel unnoticed.
